reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE is not earned. The whole target rests on a $240 price whose only evidence is that two other DTC-compliance template sellers list a similar workbook at $240. That is a competitor's list price, a benchmark of what someone else asks, not a recorded purchase by these wineries of this offer; Brain's own planner holds OFFER_AND_PRICE unestablished ('no single price on the card') and flags the reconstruction implausible. The conversion fact (18 paid of 150) states no price it was measured at, so it cannot stand in for the price either. With price unestablished, the stance should be CONDITIONAL: a live offer at $240 to a first tranche of directory contacts, with proof/stop/continue thresholds that measure paid orders at that price, before claiming the $2,500.
findings: Arithmetic as written: 12 x $240 = $2,880 gross, 12 x $4 = $48 cost, net $2,832; ceil(2500/240)=11 deals; at 18/150 = 12% conversion, 12 deals need 100 contacts, plan emails 150 (expected 18). Payouts day 8 and day 15 inside 30 days. The arithmetic is internally consistent, but every dollar of it multiplies the unestablished $240.

Price: 'Two DTC-compliance template sellers list ... at $240 (listing pages)' is what other sellers charge, not what this buyer pays for this offer (NOT_A_PURCHASE). The revision's disagreement treats a listing as 'a published price buyers pay' — a listing shows an asking price, not a purchase.
Conversion 18/150 is recorded without the price it was measured at; it does not establish $240.

Executor capabilities SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED and the card-payment collection step has no connected provider; the plan should name this as a setup prerequisite rather than present the steps as routine.

Brain's step list assigns Deliver to PERSON with 0.5 human hours per deal (card humanHours 0.5); the revision's member ownerHours is null and the deliver step says BRAIN. With 12 deals that is ~6 owner hours unaccounted for; no hours ceiling is set, but the ledger should match.
Harvest-crew alternative correctly excluded: $22 is a worker's hourly wage (not a placement fee a vineyard pays) and 61 deals against 60 once-a-season buyers fails volume.

Suggested revision: stance CONDITIONAL; validation decides OFFER_AND_PRICE on cop_52cc540b8d5040aaaa5b — offer the workbook at $240 to the first ~50 directory contacts; proof = >=4 card-paid orders at $240 within 7 days (carries 11 deals from the remaining 360 contacts at the measured rate); stop if <2 paid; continue to the full list on proof.

conditions.why: The price fact is two other sellers' listing pages at $240 — an asking price by competitors, not a purchase price these wineries are recorded paying for this offer.

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is now the right stance and the plan is startable. The $240 is correctly held as ASSUMED with the price buyers pay UNKNOWN, OFFER_AND_PRICE is marked missing and is the one link the live test decides. Every other link is evidenced (410 directory wineries, 18/150 paid conversion on this offer, Brain-proven spreadsheet fulfilment, $4 cost, 5-day payout, zero capital). The test takes orders only for a deliverable Brain has proven, setup of sender and payment link is named first, and passing at the threshold carries the target inside 30 days.
findings: Recomputed: ceil(2500/240) = 11 deals; plan sells 12 = $2,880 gross, $48 cost, $2,832 net. Ledger: 3 x $240 = $720 settling day 12, 9 x $240 = $2,160 settling day 22; deliver cost 12 x $4 = $48. Matches the check trace.
Threshold carries the target: proof = 3 paid of 50 (6%). At exactly 6%, the remaining 360 wineries yield ~21, so 3 + 21 = 24 >= 11 needed; orders by day 17 settle by day 22 <= 30.
Stop rule: <3 paid at $240 by day 7 stops and re-plans at a researched price; nothing is committed before proof ($12 of direct cost, paid from receipts).
The rebuttal on owner hours is acceptable here: the card names Brain as producer, and the goal sets no hours ceiling.
Carry forward: re-measure the second-wave rate from the $240 test rather than the unpriced 18/150.

validation.proof: At least 3 of the first 50 directory wineries pay $240 by card for the workbook by day 7.

review.reasons: CONDITIONAL is now the right stance and the plan is startable. The $240 is correctly held as ASSUMED with the price buyers pay UNKNOWN, OFFER_AND_PRICE is marked missing and is the one link the live test decides. Every other link is evidenced (410 directory wineries, 18/150 paid conversion on this offer, Brain-proven spreadsheet fulfilment, $4 cost, 5-day payout, zero capital). The test takes orders only for a deliverable Brain has proven, setup of sender and payment link is named first, and passing at the threshold carries the target inside 30 days.
findings: Recomputed: ceil(2500/240) = 11 deals; plan sells 12 = $2,880 gross, $48 cost, $2,832 net. Ledger: 3 x $240 = $720 settling day 12, 9 x $240 = $2,160 settling day 22; deliver cost 12 x $4 = $48. Matches the check trace.
Threshold carries the target: proof = 3 paid of 50 (6%). At exactly 6%, the remaining 360 wineries yield ~21, so 3 + 21 = 24 >= 11 needed; orders by day 17 settle by day 22 <= 30.
Stop rule: <3 paid at $240 by day 7 stops and re-plans at a researched price; nothing is committed before proof ($12 of direct cost, paid from receipts).
The rebuttal on owner hours is acceptable here: the card names Brain as producer, and the goal sets no hours ceiling.
Carry forward: re-measure the second-wave rate from the $240 test rather than the unpriced 18/150.
